_about: Component spec for pos-number-selector (style/pos-number-selector.css, js/pos-number-selector.js, partial forms/number-selector.liquid) — created 2026-10-31 from the design approved in tools/component-wizard.html. Single source of truth for the Variants/Usage/Tokens tabs on /style-guide "Number selector" section and for AI-assisted generation. One variant; six states (normal, hover, focus, filled, disabled, display-only) and the error / success intents of the text input, with the same state keys as text-input.json (error, error-filled, error-hover …). Every token is the one the CSS applies; Figma names looked up per RULES.md 6.4 (figma: null where no mapping exists). Regenerate spec-number-selector.liquid with the RULES.md 6.4 snippet after any change here — never hand-edit the .liquid partial.
name: Number selector
description: A number field with decrease / increase stepper buttons in one frame, for small whole-number values such as a quantity. Built on the input field tokens and the same states as the text input.
whenToUse: Choosing a small whole number where stepping by one is common — a quantity, a number of guests, a count of items.
The value has a sensible starting point and clear limits (min / max).
Add readonly to show the value as display only — transparent background, the stepper buttons stay in place but are inactive.
whenNotToUse: The range is large or the value is rarely changed by small steps (a year, a price) — use a text input with inputmode="numeric" instead.
The value is picked from a continuous range where the exact number matters less — use a slider instead.
The user picks one of a few named options — use a select, radio buttons or a segmented button instead.
do: Always associate a visible <label> with the input via matching for and id, and pass the same label to the partial so the buttons are named after it ("Decrease quantity").
Set min, max and step — the stepper button at a limit turns inactive automatically.
Give a sensible starting value; the field turns bold (filled) once the value differs from it.
For errors pass intent: 'error' (sets aria-invalid="true") + .pos-form-error, for success intent: 'success' (aria-invalid="false") + .pos-form-success, the same frames as the text input.
dont: Use a placeholder instead of a starting value — the field always shows a number; an emptied field returns to its starting value when it loses focus.
Make the stepper buttons focusable separately — the arrow keys on the number do the same, one Tab stop per field like every other input.
Style the component outside the .pos-form wrapper.
accessibility: The number is a native <input type="number"> (a spin button): ↑ / ↓ step the value, typing works, screen readers announce the value.
The stepper buttons have tabindex="-1" and aria-controls pointing at the input; their accessible names include the field label.
After a button press the field label and the new value are announced ("Quantity 7") through a polite live region inside the component.
Error and success messages should be linked via aria-describedby; required fields use the required attribute.

props.name: id
props.description: Id of the number input — the <label for> and the buttons' aria-controls point at it.

props.name: label
props.description: The field label, used in the stepper buttons' names ("Decrease quantity" / "Increase quantity"); falls back to "value" when not passed — always pass it when the field has a label. The live region reads the visible <label> text (or the input's aria-label) with the value ("Quantity 7").

props.name: value
props.description: Starting value. The field shows it in regular weight and turns bold (filled) once the value differs from it.

props.name: min / max / step
props.description: Native number-input limits and step. At a limit the matching stepper button is disabled.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Disables the input and both buttons — not-allowed cursor over the whole field.

props.name: readonly
props.description: Display only: transparent background, regular text, buttons visible but inactive.

props.name: intent
props.description: Sets aria-invalid="true" / "false" on the number: the error / success frame of the text input. Pair it with .pos-form-error / .pos-form-success linked via describedby.
